note: Coordinates are NASA Mars Trek waypoint/path vertices (degrees, Mars body). Easting/northing are the same points transformed to the site's Mars equirectangular CRS. science_value (0..1) and minutes_on_target are scenario design choices [tunable], not NASA measurements.

crew.name: EVA start
crew.source: Mars Trek curiosity_path vertex 6300 (the traverse point 138 m north of Pahrump Hills); projected with the site Mars CRS

targets.name: Pahrump Hills
targets.why: Oldest exposed Murray formation at the base of Mount Sharp. Jarosite at the Mojave drill site points to acidic water, so this outcrop records early fluid chemistry and habitability.
targets.source: NASA Mars Trek curiosity_waypoints FID 5 (Pahrump Hills); feature text: https://trek.nasa.gov/mars/jpl/assets/features/curiosity/pahrump_hills.html

targets.name: Marias Pass
targets.why: Murray–Stimson contact. Bright halos around fractures are enriched in silica, recording fluid movement through the rock after deposition.
targets.source: NASA Mars Trek curiosity_waypoints FID 6 (Marias Pass); feature text: https://trek.nasa.gov/mars/jpl/assets/features/curiosity/marias_pass.html

targets.name: Vera Rubin Ridge
targets.why: CRISM observed a hematite-rich ridge. This iron oxide forms in association with water, so the ridge can constrain redox conditions and past habitability.
targets.source: NASA Mars Trek curiosity_waypoints FID 11 (Vera Rubin Ridge); feature text: https://trek.nasa.gov/mars/jpl/assets/features/curiosity/vera_rubin_ridge.html
